name: p140-full-batch01-payloads-001-003
classification: Legacy successful terminal experimental batch, explicitly unselected; no modern sealed lifecycle fabricated.

semantics.scope: This is preservation of historical unqualified experimental bytes, not a new correctness claim. Every selected byte matches its original product and transport receipt.

compressionEvidence.status: Extrapolation only; selected files have not been compressed. The exact cap, if capture succeeds, yields the stated lower bound.

captureDesign.method: Bounded streaming gzip/tar capture followed by unchanged archive-v02 full member verification and exact-file plan. Source files remain untouched until separately authorized apply.
captureDesign.compatibility: Existing Phase169 helper allows only program.ssa/s/o and Phase173 retired adapter permits only its pinned API/source list. Neither directly admits these nested payload.bin leaves. close.capsule reserves raw size+16 MiB and would over-admit scratch for this streaming case; use an explicitly reviewed capped-output capture, without relaxing the maintained verifier.
captureDesign.scope: Exactly three named payloads. All other files and directory entries remain hot. No whole-folder pruning.

dependencyAudit.method: Read-only streaming literal root-reference scan, plus actual writer/transport receipt review. Current bindings explicitly name their source/API/IR inputs; none names this retired batch. Dynamic historical --prior-manifest workflows require restoration.
dependencyAudit.limits: Root must recheck new active manifests and source requests immediately before capture/apply. No claim that historical Phase140 commands can run without restoration.

openDescriptorCheck.scope: Accessible current-user processes only; no unrelated descriptor targets or commands recorded.

all executables, native/compiler sources, APIs, runtime/toolchain objects, profiles and source evidence

every Phase173 artifact, especially active plan-capture-binary03, current automatic/owned-decomposition and all ABI/dispatch/borrow/AST/digest inputs
all unlisted paths and the shared Phase32 execution lock
